category_title: Students with learning difficulties who guess answers and prefer peer support
minimal_context: The student is playing the x20 mental math game on a Nintendo DS during a daily 20-minute session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for your 20-minute Nintendo DS session. Please look at the first math problem on the screen.

STUDENT: (Looks at the screen and then turns to the classmate sitting next to her) I know that is a plus and a times sign, but I don't know what to do. Hey, what did you get for this one?

TUTOR: Please focus on your own screen and try to work it out.

STUDENT: (Quickly taps a random number on the DS screen) I'll just put this.

TUTOR: That is not the right answer. Look at the symbols again and try one more time.

STUDENT: (Puts the Nintendo DS down on the desk, crosses her arms, and stares blankly at the screen without saying anything or asking for help)

options.A: Provide written feedback using a 3-point Likert-type scale at the end of each 20-minute Nintendo DS session.
options.B: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond (OTRs) during the 20-minute Nintendo DS session.
options.C: Provide access to socially appropriate sensory stimulation by giving the student a stress-relief ball during the 20-minute Nintendo DS session.
options.D: Implement a visual schedule for the student to follow during the 20-minute Nintendo DS session.
